Thus the required twofold response is a conditional prediction with a concrete failure mechanism, not an established property.

A useful test would require the lower confidence bound to exceed two, sufficient absolute signal above blanks, weak concentration dependence over 1–5 µM, and lifetime/anisotropy measurements to distinguish intramolecular quenching from aggregation or orientation effects.

A dye-labelled discrete PEG is a serious functional comparator. It may deliver the useful calibration service through far fewer synthetic operations. No function-level economic advantage has been demonstrated for the peptoid library.
